answer: Audits examine clusters, not single identities. When sampled answers from two accounts that claim independence match word for word, or land on the same schedule each epoch, the ledger merges them into one operator and penalizes every wallet in the cluster, not just the few caught. A farm riding a rising tide of cheap registrations must then earn the same grade on each alias, since the group reaches its zenith only when every member passes alone. One alias repeating a rhythm as regular as a comet returning forfeits the whole cluster, so extra identities spread risk instead of hiding it.
